items.name: Nao Higano
items.short: Japanese soprano from Chiba. She studied opera and concert singing in Japan and at the Academy of Performing Arts in Bratislava, where she completed doctoral studies and earned the ArtD. degree.

content.text: Nao Higano is a soprano from Chiba, Japan. She studied opera and concert singing at Seitoku University and at the Department of Voice of the Academy of Performing Arts in Bratislava, where she completed doctoral studies under Prof. Peter Mikuláš and earned the ArtD. degree.
She took part in numerous international masterclasses with teachers including P. de Neapoli, D. Iordachescu, Y. Hayashi, M. Janková, G. Beňačková, S. Kopčák, P. Dvorský, Z. Livorová and V. Chmelo.

She has successfully appeared at international music festivals and has recorded for radio and television broadcasters including ORF, Hungarian Radio, Czech Radio, Slovak Radio, Czech Television and Slovak Television, as well as for music publishers.

In solo recitals she performs song and chamber repertoire as well as oratorio, mass and cantata literature. Her repertoire ranges from the Renaissance to music of the 21st century, with particular attention to Slavic compositions.
She was a member of the chamber trio Sen Tegmento, founded by clarinettist Martin Adámek, a soloist and member of Ensemble Intercontemporain in Paris.

She has collaborated with numerous orchestras and chamber ensembles, including the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra, Slovak Philharmonic, Bohdan Warchal Slovak Chamber Orchestra, Slovak Radio Symphony Orchestra, Czech Radio Symphony Orchestra, State Philharmonic Košice, Slovak Sinfonietta Žilina, Capella Istropolitana, Moyzes Quartet and Bohuslav Martinů Philharmonic.

She prepared a song recital for Prague’s Rudolfinum and has performed at the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam. She received first prize from the Yamaha Foundation and several awards from the Music Fund in Bratislava.

As a soloist she has appeared as a guest at the Slovak National Theatre Opera in Bratislava, the National Theatre Brno, the National Theatre Prague, the State Opera in Banská Bystrica and the opera in Košice.
She achieved particular success in the role of the Woman in Arnold Schoenberg’s Erwartung at its Slovak premiere at the SND Opera in 2002.

In recent years she has also developed as a visual artist, exhibiting her work in Czechia, Slovakia and abroad. She is an honorary member of Rotary Club Kroměříž, with which she participates in charity concerts.

items.name: Gorin
items.short: A group dedicated to samurai culture, historical martial traditions and the Sengoku period.
items.description: Visitors can look forward to demonstrations of archery, combat, tameshigiri and stories about samurai and their traditions.

content.text: Gorin will bring the atmosphere of samurai Japan to Považská Bystrica and present weapons, traditions and historical martial techniques.
Archery, combat and tameshigiri
The programme will include demonstrations of archery, combat and tameshigiri – the traditional practice of test cutting with a sword.

items.name: Noriko Komiyama
items.short: A Japanese instructor of Sōgetsu ikebana. She will present the differences between the Ikenobō and Sōgetsu schools and demonstrate Japanese flower arrangement.

content.text: Noriko Komiyama is a Japanese ikebana instructor who has lived in Prague for many years. She focuses mainly on the Sōgetsu school and regularly shares her experience through public demonstrations and workshops.

Her ikebana demonstrations have also taken place under the patronage of the Embassy of Japan, for example during the Flora Bratislava exhibition, where she led practical workshops in addition to a stage demonstration.
Ikebana does not have to start with an exotic flower

At Japan Day, she will show how ordinary flowers and plants available in our surroundings can also be used. She will also introduce the different approaches of two major ikebana schools – Ikenobō and Sōgetsu.
Visitors will see how even simple, readily available plants can be turned into an impressive Japanese composition that they can later try creating at home.

items.name: Ing. Martin Labudík
items.short: Founder of Nagomi tea and lecturer on Japanese tea.
items.description: He will present the diversity of Japanese tea, its preparation, work on a tea farm in Japan, and the topic of green tea and antioxidants.

content.text: Martin Labudík from Nagomi tea will introduce different categories of Japanese tea and demonstrate practical preparation methods.
From the tea farm to the cup
He will also talk about working on a tea farm in Japan, tea processing, and what we currently know about antioxidants, oxidative stress and the use of tea in skincare.

items.name: Silvestr Prajer
items.short: Demonstrations of samurai martial arts, kyūjutsu and tameshigiri.
items.description: Silvestr founded an iaidō and kendō group in Plzeň in 1994. Over time, they progressed from demonstrations of the use of the Japanese sword and other weapons to full-armour samurai combat, demonstrations of kyūjutsu – combat archery – and tameshigiri, or test cutting. In Japanese history, they were particularly inspired by the Sengoku jidai, the period of warring clans, when martial arts developed to an extraordinary level.

items.name: Hisayo Yasuda
items.short: A Japanese language and culture instructor who will present the traditional Japanese art of origami.

content.text: Hisayo Yasuda is a Japanese language instructor who has lived in Bratislava for many years. She teaches Japanese and introduces Japanese culture to the public. Her activities also include origami workshops and demonstrations at public events and in her work with children at primary schools.

Origami is the traditional Japanese art of paper folding. At Japan Day, Hisayo will show step by step how colourful origami paper can be turned into various small objects and figures – from simpler hearts, balloons and boxes to the traditional crane.
Her origami demonstrations are also part of the Cherry Blossom Festival – Sakura Festival, organised by the Embassy of Japan in Slovakia.

Hisayo guides her workshops patiently, step by step, so complete beginners can also take part. The aim is not only to create an attractive paper model, but also to discover one aspect of Japanese culture through origami.
Let’s have fun together making cute little items using colourful origami paper.

items.name: Mgr. Akiko Komura, Ph.D.
items.short: A Japanese academic and university lecturer who will introduce the traditional Japanese art of shodō calligraphy.

content.text: Mgr. Akiko Komura, Ph.D. works as a university lecturer at the Department of East Asian Studies, Faculty of Arts, Comenius University in Bratislava. In her academic work, she focuses on topics related to Japan, its society, culture and traditions.

At Japan Day, she will introduce shodō – the traditional Japanese art of calligraphy. She will explain its significance in Japanese culture, the basic principles of brushwork and how individual characters are created.
The programme will include not only a lecture but also a practical workshop. Participants will be able to try using a Japanese calligraphy brush and create their own character.

The workshop will offer an opportunity to discover Japanese calligraphy not only as a form of writing, but also as a traditional artistic discipline combining precision of movement, concentration and aesthetics.

items.name: Judo Považská Bystrica
items.short: Demonstrations of judo and Japanese martial arts.
items.description: Further programme details will be added later.

items.name: Jana Michalková
items.short: Discover daylily growing and breeding, their place in the garden, and their lesser-known culinary uses.

content.text: I have been growing daylilies since 2010, when I ordered my first ten plants. It was love at first sight, as soon as the first flowers bloomed. My collection gradually grew to around 400 varieties.

I studied daylilies extensively and later began experimenting with cross-breeding to develop my own cultivars. Meeting Martin Kamenský was a great help to me. He worked on daylily breeding for about 40 years in the USA and continues this work in Slovakia.

In 2020, we co-founded Hemerocallis Slovensko, a civic association bringing together daylily growers and admirers. Our goal is to encourage the cultivation of these undemanding yet remarkably beautiful perennials throughout Slovakia.
Few people know that daylily flowers are edible. They can be used in salads or as dessert decorations, for example.
At our presentation stand, I will be happy to advise visitors on growing daylilies and choosing suitable cultivars.

items.name: Mgr. Ivana Mičkalová
items.short: A demonstration of the traditional Japanese kumihimo technique – braiding decorative and functional cords.

content.text: Mgr. Ivana Mičkalová practises the traditional Japanese technique of kumihimo, the braiding of decorative and functional cords. She was introduced to Japanese culture through the Gorin samurai show group, whose performance she first attended in 2015. Gradually, she became part of the group’s circle and developed a deeper interest in traditional Japanese crafts.

She discovered kumihimo thanks to members of Gorin who worked with the traditional marudai and takadai braiding stands. She was fascinated by the precision of the technique and by the way individual strands gradually form complex decorative patterns.

Since 2022, she has been demonstrating kumihimo at public events and teaching the basics of the technique to interested participants. She began with simpler patterns and gradually expanded her experience, knowledge and work with specialist literature.

At Japan Day, she will introduce visitors to the traditional technique of braiding Japanese cords and show how kumihimo is created in practice. Visitors will be able to observe the method of working with the cords and learn more about a craft with a long tradition in Japanese culture.

items.name: Aiko Bosák
items.short: She will present the making of badges from Japanese fabrics and a selection of traditional Japanese kimono.

content.text: Aiko Bosák will show visitors how small decorative badges are made from Japanese fabrics and textiles.
Her presentation will also include a selection of Japanese kimono for sale and an opportunity to discover traditional Japanese textiles, patterns and their uses.
At Japan Day, visitors will be able to see finished products, Japanese fabrics and kimono directly at the venue.

items.name: Asuka Emura
items.short: She will present the traditional Japanese art of paper folding – origami.

content.text: Asuka Emura will introduce visitors to origami – the traditional Japanese art of paper folding.
She will show how a simple square of paper can gradually be folded into different shapes, objects and figures.
Visitors will be able to discover one of Japan’s best-known creative traditions and try the basic principles of origami themselves.

items.name: Satoko Kino
items.short: She will present Japanese tea, gastronomy and everyday dining culture from a Japanese perspective.

content.text: Satoko Kino comes from Japan and has long been involved in introducing Japanese culture, gastronomy and everyday traditions in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. She is associated with the Nagomi brand, which focuses on Japanese tea and other products from Japan.

At Japan Day, she will introduce Japanese tea and gastronomy from the perspective of someone who grew up with Japanese culture. She will explain how tea and food naturally appear in everyday life in Japan, how they are served and what role they play in shared meals and hospitality.

The presentation will also include practical demonstrations and tastings. Visitors will be able to discover the flavours of Japan and learn more about the differences between how Japanese tea and food are perceived in Europe and how they form part of everyday life in Japan.
